question: Can fixed effective voltage filtering explain recovery waveforms, and do history models improve held-out predictions?
scope: Same source and two targets; retrospective development using previously inspected traces; no biological mechanism identification.

detector_manifest.scope: Reference detector runtime source; historical DB producer commit unverified

split.prior_exposure: Earlier analyses inspected all target traces and some summaries. Fit exclusion is computational, not blinded confirmation.

measurement.input: Detected source AP times, not target synaptic current
measurement.output: Target voltage uV relative to own pretrain[-100,-10)ms mean
measurement.bins: Exact original-lattice means of50 samples at100kHz (0.5ms); same operator on predictions
measurement.artifact_mask: Bins intersecting command onset-0.5ms through source spike+2ms are omitted from scores
measurement.regions: Initial ends spike8+18ms; gap from spike8+20ms to command9-0.5ms; recovery ends spike12+18ms; tail starts spike12+20ms
measurement.baseline: One common learned offset per model/target, fitted on initial train only; no target-outcome gain or offset refit in held-out sweeps
measurement.sign: Nonnegative kernel amplitude for excitatory source hypothesis, applied identically to unlabeled target; negative label means no reported synapse, not inhibition
measurement.holding: Zero stored DA does not include separately recorded holding settings or imply absent spontaneous input

configuration.initial_state: Depression resource1 and facilitation0 reset per sweep; assumed, not measured
configuration.selection: Lowest training MSE separately per family, equal total weight per sweep; no held-out refit
configuration.comparison: History candidates must beat both offset-only and fixed kernels on temporal initial AND recovery regions to motivate further testing; even success is not causal identification

positive.meaning: Grid sensitivity diagnostic, not a confidence set or empirical Fourier estimate; ignores fitted amplitude sign at zero.

negative.meaning: Grid sensitivity diagnostic, not a confidence set or empirical Fourier estimate; ignores fitted amplitude sign at zero.
